key_insight: Symmetry-based low-rank fine-tuning enables one MatterSim 1M potential to predict lattice thermal conductivity across compounds sharing a crystal symmetry, including compounds not used in fine-tuning.
engineering_relevance: Faster thermal-conductivity screening could support thermal management and materials selection for thermoelectric, microelectronic, and photovoltaic applications.
method: Select a small set of compounds sharing a crystal symmetry.
Fine-tune MatterSim 1M using symmetry-based few-shot low-rank adaptation.
Calculate lattice thermal conductivity by solving the Boltzmann transport equation.
evidence_signal: Across half-Heuslers (space group 216), space-group-225 materials, and spinels (227), mean absolute relative differences from moment tensor potential and polyMLP references were 2–3× smaller than for untuned MatterSim 1M; potential preparation for 100 compounds was approximately 5–7× faster than individual fine-tuning.
watch_item: Transfer is demonstrated within shared-symmetry material groups, not across arbitrary crystal structures, and the abstract reports no direct solar-cell device validation.
paper_title: Symmetry-Based Parameter Efficient Low-Rank Fine-Tuning for High-Throughput Calculation of Lattice Thermal Conductivity
